      • getTypeReferenceForParameterizedField

        public static TypeReference getTypeReferenceForParameterizedField(java.lang.Class fieldType,
                                                                  java.lang.Class elementType)
                                                           throws java.lang.ClassNotFoundException
        Builds the element TypeReference for an array-typed struct field declared via @Parameterized on a constructor parameter.

        Limitation: this annotation-based constructor-reflection path represents only one element-type level. Nested array fields (e.g. uint256[2][2] declared as StaticArray2<StaticArray2<Uint256>>) are therefore not supported by the current implementation and are rejected explicitly. Nested arrays remain supported through runtime type references, for example by placing TypeReference.makeTypeReference("uint256[2][2]") in the innerTypes list of a runtime struct reference.

        Throws:
        java.lang.ClassNotFoundException

      • validateTypeReferenceDepth

        public static void validateTypeReferenceDepth(TypeReference<?> root)
        Validates a TypeReference graph before decoding by capping its depth at MAX_TYPEREF_DEPTH. A cycle keeps increasing the depth along the cyclic path, so cycles are rejected by the same check; shared (diamond) nodes at legal depths pass. Recursion is bounded by the cap itself, so this method cannot blow the JVM stack on malicious input.

        Called from DefaultFunctionReturnDecoder.build for each output parameter (direct TypeDecoder entry points are not guarded); bounds every downstream recursive traversal of subTypeReference / innerTypes (in TypeDecoder.isDynamic, Utils.getTypeName, decodeStaticStruct, decodeDynamicStruct, etc.). All local state, no shared mutable fields — safe for concurrent invocation on the same TypeReference.
